priorities.finding: Request-context features are the only screened group with positive overall primary lift (+0.0022), positive lift on three of four days, full coverage, and the strongest within-user ranking evidence among the screened groups. GAUC is comparatively strong for cold users (0.654) and warm users/items (0.631), although nDCG@5 is weaker (0.492 and 0.508), indicating better broad ranking than top-five concentration.
priorities.recommended_action: Prioritize a small confirmatory experiment for request context only, with explicit monitoring of daily stability and nDCG@5. Apply the strict early-stop rule after this confirmation if the primary lift or top-five metric fails to improve.

avoid: Reject user-profile, historical user-author affinity, upload-recency, content-duration, item-metadata, historical-author-response, and historical-item-response groups because their overall primary lifts are negative; the historical response groups also show substantially degraded GAUC and nDCG@5 (screen:user_profile, screen:historical_user_author_affinity, screen:upload_recency, screen:content_duration, screen:item_metadata, screen:historical_author_response, screen:historical_item_response).
Do not use outcome-derived current-impression signals or aggregate snapshots without per-impression availability timestamps; they are leakage-prone and invalid for ranking-time evaluation.
metric_diagnosis: The request-context result supports stable within-user ranking more through GAUC than through top-five quality: GAUC is 0.654 for cold users and 0.631 for warm users/items, while nDCG@5 is only 0.492 and 0.508. The cold-item segment has only 8 rows and is weak (GAUC 0.5, nDCG@5 0.25), so it should not drive the decision. The positive aggregate lift is modest relative to daily variation, making confirmation and early stopping appropriate rather than broad feature expansion (screen:request_context).
